entries.title: Women in IT jobs: it is about education, but it is also about more than just education
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that by end-2016 fewer than 25 percent of information technology (IT) jobs in developed countries will be held by women
entries.metric: share of developed-country IT jobs held by women
entries.subject: Women in IT

entries.title: Trailing millennials are the pro-PC, not the post-PC, generation
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that trailing millennials (18-24 years old) are likely to be the most pro-PC of all age groups in 2016.
entries.subject: Personal computers

entries.title: Touch commerce: the mobile online checkout gets an express lane
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2016, the number of individuals who use a third party touch-based payment service to make a purchase on their mobile devices ... should increase by 150 percent, to reach 50 million regular users.
entries.metric: regular users of touch-based mobile payment for online purchases
entries.subject: Mobile payments (touch commerce)

entries.title: Graphene: research now, reap next decade
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts the total value of the graphene materials market in 2016 is likely to be in the low tens of millions of dollars
entries.subject: Graphene

entries.title: Cognitive technologies enhance enterprise software
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that by end-2016 more than 80 of the world's 100 largest enterprise software companies by revenues will have integrated cognitive technologies into their products
entries.metric: top-100 enterprise software companies with cognitive technologies
entries.subject: Cognitive technologies (AI) in enterprise software

entries.title: Virtual reality: a billion dollar niche
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that virtual reality (VR) will have its first billion dollar year in 2016, with about $700 million in hardware sales, and the remainder from content.
entries.subject: Virtual reality

entries.title: Mobile games: leading, but less lucrative
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2016 mobile devices (smartphone and tablet) will become the leading games platform by software revenue, generating $35 billion in revenue, up 20 percent from 2015.
entries.subject: Mobile games

entries.title: Mobile ad-blockers: saved by the app?
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts a mere 0.3 percent of all mobile device owners (comprising smartphones and tablets) will use an ad-blocker by end-2016.
entries.metric: share of mobile device owners using an ad-blocker
entries.subject: Ad blocking

entries.title: The award for stable box office revenues in the face of digital media goes to…
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the value of movie theater admissions in the US and Canada will fall by about three percent in 2016, to about $10.6 billion, with about 1.3 billion tickets sold.
entries.subject: Movie box office

entries.title: US TV: erosion, not implosion
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that pay-TV penetration (or reach) will fall more than two percentage points to 81 percent in 2016, to under 79 percent in 2017, and around 70 percent by 2020.
entries.subject: Pay TV cord cutting
entries.note: The prediction lists six erosion fronts with separate numbers (cord-cutting rate, penetration, bill, antenna homes, daily minutes, 18-24 viewing); the penetration figure is captured as the headline number.

entries.title: European football scores $30 billion
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the European football market may generate $30 billion (€27 billion) in revenues in 2016/2017
entries.subject: European football revenue

entries.title: eSports: bigger and smaller than you think
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that eSports will generate global revenues of $500 million in 2016, up 25 percent from about $400 million in 2015
entries.subject: eSports

entries.title: The dawn of the Gigabit Internet age: every bit counts
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the number of Gigabit per second (Gbit/s) Internet connections will surge to 10 million by year-end, a tenfold increase, of which about 70 percent will be residential connections.
entries.subject: Gigabit broadband

entries.title: Used smartphones: the $17 billion market you may never have heard of
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2016 consumers will sell outright or trade in approximately 120 million used smartphones generating more than $17 billion for their owners
entries.metric: used smartphones sold or traded in
entries.subject: Used smartphones

entries.title: The rise of the data exclusive
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2016, 26 percent of smartphone users in developed markets will not make any traditional phone calls in a given week.
entries.metric: developed-market smartphone users making no traditional calls in a week
entries.subject: Mobile voice calls

entries.title: VoLTE/VoWiFi: capacity, reach and capability
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts about 100 carriers worldwide will be offering at least one packet-based voice service by the end of 2016
entries.subject: VoLTE / VoWiFi

entries.title: Photo sharing: trillions and rising
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2016, 2.5 trillion photos will be shared or stored online, a 15 percent increase on the prior year.
entries.subject: Online photo sharing

notes: 15th edition by count from 2002. From this edition the publisher line reads 'Deloitte Global predicts'. Rank is the order in the report. Publication month from the January launch pattern; exact day not confirmed.
